Warning:
Lemma <REF_0001>
should be used with care. For example, it applies to
<MATH_0001>``flat'', <MATH_0002>``empty'',
and <MATH_0003>``flat and locally of finite presentation''. But given a
morphism of algebraic spaces <MATH_0004> the largest open
subspace <MATH_0005> such that <MATH_0006> is flat is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>not<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> the set of points
where <MATH_0007> is flat!

Notwithstanding the warning in
Remark <REF_0001>
there are some cases where
Lemma <REF_0002>
can be used without causing ambiguity.
We give a list. In each case we omit the verification of
assumptions (1) and (2) and we give references which imply
(3) and (4). Here is the list:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002>
<LOCKED_0001>
<MATH_0001>``locally of finite type'', <MATH_0002>,
and <MATH_0003>``relative dimension <MATH_0004>''.
See
Morphisms of Spaces,
Definition <REF_0003>
and
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemmas
<REF_0004> and
<REF_0005>.
<STRUCT_0003>
<LOCKED_0002>
<MATH_0005>``locally of finite type'', <MATH_0006>,
and <MATH_0007>``locally quasi-finite''.
This is the case <MATH_0008> of the previous item, see
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0006>.
On the other hand, properties (3) and (4) are spelled out in
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0007>.
<STRUCT_0004>
<LOCKED_0003>
<MATH_0009>``locally of finite type'', <MATH_0010>,
and <MATH_0011>``unramified''. This is
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0008>.
<STRUCT_0005>
<LOCKED_0004>
<MATH_0012>``locally of finite presentation'',
<MATH_0013>``flat and locally of finite presentation'', and
<MATH_0014>``flat''. See
More on Morphisms of Spaces, Theorem
<REF_0009> and
Lemma <REF_0010>.
Note that here <MATH_0015> is always exactly the set of points
where the morphism <MATH_0016> is flat because we only consider this open
when <MATH_0017> has <MATH_0018> (see loc.cit.).
<STRUCT_0006>
<LOCKED_0005>
<MATH_0019>``locally of finite presentation'',
<MATH_0020>``flat and locally of finite presentation'', and
<MATH_0021>``<ACCENT_0001>tale''. This follows on combining
(<REF_0011>) and (<REF_0012>) because an unramified
morphism which is flat and locally of finite presentation is <ACCENT_0002>tale, see
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0013>.
<STRUCT_0007> Add more here as needed (compare with the longer list at
More on Groupoids, Remark <REF_0014>).
<STRUCT_0008>
